# Alibre Fillet R&D

- Alibre Fillet R&D is a set of experimental apps for inspecting the edge and fillet geometry of a part, written to explore what the Alibre automation API exposes.
  - What it does
    - Attaches to a part that is already open in Alibre Design.
    - Walks the bodies, faces, and edges of that part and selects them in the live session so you can see what it found.
    - Reports the underlying curve for each edge, covering lines, circles, arcs, ellipses, B-splines, and points.
    - Lists the 2D and 3D sketches in the part along with the kind of figures they contain.
    - Offers the same workflow through a console app, a WPF window, and a Windows Forms inspector.
    - Includes sample parts for testing full-round fillet geometry.
  - What you need
    - Alibre Design installed and running with a part open.
    - The .NET Framework 4.8.1 runtime on 64-bit Windows.
  - Getting started
    - Build `source/Fillet_R&D.sln` in Release configuration.
    - Open one of the sample parts in Alibre Design.
    - Run whichever of the three front ends you prefer.
  - Where things live
    - `source/` holds the three VB.NET projects and the sample parts.
    - `documentation/` holds reference notes.
    - `reviews/` holds dated code reviews.
  - Good to know
    - This is exploratory code rather than a finished tool, so expect rough edges.
    - The variable-radius fillet call is scaffolded but switched off, so nothing is written to your part.
  - Use it under the MIT License.
